title: ≤0.100.x clients can never detect v0.101.x — 4-part release tag unparseable by old VersionHelper (silent "up to date")

status.label: Legacy-client update reachability plan needed
status.detail: The incompatibility is substantiated; release-side bridge versus manual-upgrade mitigation needs validation.

judgment.rationale: The issue and automated diagnostic summary identify a concrete compatibility gap: ≤0.100.x clients parse only three version components, while later official release tags use four; parse failure leaves the update result at “up to date.” PR #49414 introduced the new format after 0.100.2 shipped. Those binaries cannot be patched in place, so remediation must be a release/channel bridge or explicit manual-upgrade path.
evidence: Reporter uses 0.100.2 Stable and describes Settings saying up-to-date when the release API returns v0.101.2362.0.
The diagnostic archive summary says UpdateState.json confirms an update check ran and reported current without an error.
Automated triage confirms the old parser only accepts three components.
Merged PR #49414 (2026-08-06) documents the 4-part MSI-safe release version scheme, after 0.100.2 shipped.
Latest Stable is v0.101.2362.0; latest Preview is v0.102.2911.0.
judgment.recommended_action: Test update reachability from an actual 0.100.x client; determine whether a three-part bridge release is viable, otherwise provide a clear manual upgrade path.

fix_assessment.rationale: The cause is credibly identified, but shipped clients cannot receive a code change through the current updater; the proposed remediation is a release-level bridge/manual-upgrade plan whose feasibility needs maintainer validation.

proposed_fixes.title: Restore an upgrade path for pre-0.101 clients
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Clients shipped before 4-part version support treat the current 4-part release tag as unparsable, and their update check silently retains the installed version. A current-source parser change alone cannot repair those installed binaries.
plan: Reproduce the update check with a clean 0.100.2 client and current stable metadata; verify parser failure and the up-to-date result.

Ask release engineering whether a higher three-part compatibility bridge release can be safely upgraded by affected clients; if not, publish direct manual-upgrade guidance through release notes/documentation.
Validate the chosen route from 0.100.2 through to current stable, including version ordering, install behavior, and subsequent 4-part update checks.
verification: Run an update check from unmodified 0.100.2 against current official metadata and record the result.
If a bridge is selected, verify old client offers/installs it and bridged client recognizes a current 4-part release.
If no bridge is feasible, verify official manual-upgrade instructions point to a signed current installer and explain legacy update detection.

confidence.rationale: The parser/tag mismatch is supported by the diagnostic summary and merged versioning PR; bridge-release feasibility is unverified.

issue_context.summary: A 0.100.2 installation reportedly misses the current update because its shipped parser cannot read the four-part tag introduced after that build.
known_information: PowerToys 0.100.2 Stable, GitHub installation, system installation, not elevated.
Reporter says the release API returns v0.101.2362.0 while Settings says up-to-date.
Diagnostic summary says update check ran and returned current without an error.
Reporter cites VersionHelper::fromString and PR #49414; the merged PR documents the 4-part release format.
No user comments, assignee, duplicate link, or linked fix are present.
Latest Stable is v0.101.2362.0; latest Preview is v0.102.2911.0.
inferences: The failure is consistent with the reported parser analysis; no independent execution on a 0.100.x binary was performed in this pass.
A current parser fix cannot update a client unable to discover the release; immediate mitigation is distribution/manual guidance.
No release-policy decision about a bridge is recorded.
issue_context.analysis: The issue supplies diagnostic confirmation and PR #49414 corroborates when the new format was introduced. Since an old binary cannot be remotely patched and current Stable still uses a four-part tag, the maintainer action is to test reachability and decide a release-level migration, not request more logs.
initial_investigation: Read the full issue and one automated triage comment, including diagnostic summary, API example, environment, and updatedAt.
Verified PR #49414 is merged and documents the 4-part MSI-safe version scheme; it merged after 0.100.2 shipped.
Checked live releases: v0.101.2362.0 is Latest Stable; v0.102.2911.0 is Preview.
No linked issue or fix was identified in the live thread.
